title: Guarding main: Branch Protection, Reviews & Hooks

questions.prompt: What do branch protection rules do?

options.text: Enforce conditions before changes reach a branch (e.g. require a PR, approvals, passing checks) on the server, so contributors can't bypass them
Make the branch read-only to everyone forever

questions.explanation: Branch protection is a server-side gate: it can require pull requests, reviews, and passing status checks, and block force-pushes — rules contributors cannot skip.

questions.prompt: When does a pre-commit hook run?

options.text: On the server after a push
Locally, before a commit is created — and it can abort the commit
Only when merging a pull request

questions.explanation: A pre-commit hook runs on your machine just before the commit is created; if it exits non-zero (e.g. lint fails), the commit is aborted.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Branch protection can require passing status checks before merge
A CODEOWNERS file can require review from specific owners
Client-side hooks can be bypassed with --no-verify
Client-side hooks are automatically shared with everyone who clones

questions.explanation: Branch protection can require green checks, CODEOWNERS routes required reviews, and hooks can be skipped with --no-verify. Hooks in .git/hooks are local and NOT shared by cloning.

questions.prompt: A ______ file maps paths to the people whose review is required for changes there.
questions.explanation: A CODEOWNERS file assigns owners to file paths, so PRs touching those paths require the owners' review.

questions.prompt: Why are client-side pre-commit hooks NOT a reliable enforcement mechanism?

options.text: They are local, not shared by default, and can be skipped with --no-verify
They require a paid GitHub plan

questions.explanation: Hooks live locally, don't travel with a clone unless installed, and can be bypassed with --no-verify. True enforcement needs server-side branch protection and required CI.

questions.prompt: Match each mechanism to what it is.

pairs.right: Local script run before a commit

questions.explanation: Branch protection enforces server-side, required reviews gate merges, CODEOWNERS routes reviewers, and a pre-commit hook gives local pre-commit feedback.
